steps.text: In a large saucepan over medium high heat, fry the bacon until crisp, about 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels, reserving the bacon fat in the pan, crumble and set aside.
In the same saucepan with the bacon fat, saute the onion and potatoes for 3 to 5 minutes. Sprinkle with the flour and stir well to coat.
Pour in the clam juice, bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.

Add the half-and-half and minced clams and season with salt and pepper to taste. Finally, whisk in the heavy cream, if desired. Allow to heat through, about 5 minutes. Garnish with the parsley and crumbled bacon. (Note: Do not boil if adding cream.)

raw_recipe.headline: New England Clam Chowder II
raw_recipe.description: Bottled clam juice is the secret ingredient for this extra-flavorful chowder. Otherwise, this is a fairly standard chowder recipe with lots of potatoes, bacon, and onions.

review.reviewBody:
This is a great recipe for when you're craving clam chowder, and don't want to wait. Here in Rhode Island, we have an abundance of clams, so I make this one often, using quahogs that my boys dig up. 

My one issue with this recipe, as-is, is that you have to make sure that the flour is adequately cooked, or you get that raw-flour taste. In order to do this with the sautee-the-flour-with-the-potatoes method, you run the risk of making the potatoes a bit mushy. If you have a bit more time, make a roux by melting a 1/2 stick of butter and cooking the flour in it for about 5 minutes. Wisk the roux in with the dairy before proceeding with step 4. You'll have a creamy and nicely thickened chowder with no lumps!

I doubled this recipe but I used a whole 5 pound bag of potatoes. I adapted this recipe to the crockpot. I just cubed the raw potatoes and covered them with the clam juice and the four cans of minced clams (also with the juice that was in the can with the clams) and one can of organic chicken broth. That cooked on low all day until I came home from work and finished it. I did a quick mash with an old fashioned potato mashed for a chunky soup, then added in the bacon, sauteed onion (along with fresh garlic and chopped fresh carrots.) I didn't have any cream on hand, I used one can of fat free evaporated milk instead. After tasting it, I added a little red pepper flake. This was good but I wish it was more clammy. I was quite impressed I could make this in the crockpot and now that I know I can, I don't know what's stopping me from doing that from now on. Next time, I'll make this the same way only I'll add even more minced clams and clam juice.

Made a diabetic-friendly (low carbohydrate) version by using a few substitutes, but kept to the cooking method prescribed. Subbed in diced cauliflower & turnip ( 1/2 & 1/2) mix for potatoes, and left out the flour. Made my own 1/2 & 1/2 using unsweetened almond milk & heavy cream. Used 1 entire yellow onion and a large stalk of diced celery. Used my hand blender wand to purée some of the veggies before adding the 1/2 & 1/2, to thicken the soup (because no flour). This was good soup, but not quite clammy enough for our taste. Next time, and there will be many next times, I’ll use an extra can of clams.

First time making this recipe. My wife does not eat meat, so could not use the bacon grease (used a bit of butter and oil instead) to sauté onion and potato with flour mixture. I cut a few too many potatoes, so had to use a bit more flour, and when boiling used one jar of clam juice and 1 1/2 jars (same bottle) water. I used 1 cup 1/2 & 1/2, 1/2 cup skim milk (ran out of 1/2 & 1/2) and one full cup of heavy cream. I also used four, instead of two cans of minced clams. Excellent consistency, just how we like it - thick, but still soup/chowder. Very happy with this recipe.

Subbed arrowroot powder for the flour to make it GF. Also bought Napolean brand smoked clams on accident but it added such a great element of flavor! I rinsed them first. Doubled clam juice and half and half. Yum! 12/11/16 Hubby told me tonight he doesn't like smoked clams. Also no flour or AR powder - just blended up half the potatoes for thickness.

Made as written the first time. Not bad, but not clam chowder either. Second time, doubled the clams, added some celery with the onion, skipped the flour (didn't need it) I used all the clam juice in all the cans, with came to just over a cup and a half, and puréed about 1/4 cup of the potato soup before adding it back in with the clams. Also skipped the cream at the end. Much better clam flavor. Would give that at least 4 stars.

Instead of bacon, I used 4oz diced pancetta. Cooked it till it was crispy, drained it on paper towels and kept ALL grease/oil leftover from the pancetta in the pot. Cooked the onion and only 3 small diced potatoes (used russet). I didn't need the bottle of clam juice because I used the juice from the minced cans instead. Used 1 cup heavy cream + 3/4 cup skim milk. Came out chunky/creamy the way we like it. Added a few dashes of old bay seasoning along with salt and pepper. Loved it - so did our 14 year old who doesn't like seafood.

Delicious chowder. I used bacon bits in the first step to save the work (: Rather than add the flour to potatoes, to prevent mushiness I whisked the flour into the half and half...(I actually used evaporated milk since we had no half and half) I chopped celery and added it to potatoes and onion which I sauteed in olive oil. Instead of heavy cream I used 1% milk and butter so I doubled the flour to 2T. Clam juice is a must. I tried on my second batch to use chicken broth as a substitute since I had no juice. It wasn't the same even though I used 3 cans of clams. Also pour the juice from the canned clams right in. Yummy!

using the close to same recipe and ingredients... add 2 pounds of cod,a lil celery,a can of crab meat,a can of medium shrimp...saute onoins and celery with a stick of butter, at the end add about a 1/3 cup of flour...stir... ,pour in fish stock or chicken stock add potatoes with a few cups of water to help boil the potatoes..when the potatoes are cooked firm loose the extreme heat, add Fish simmer a minute and a quart of heavy cream and maybe a little milk to you desire! this is winging it Sea food chowder!

I made this for my family and it was a hit. I made some slight changes such as adding two chopped carrots, using baby clams (whole, not minced and with liquid) and cooking for a bit longer. I always don't like it when there is not enough clams, so I used around 20oz. in the entire pot, and it was perfect. I also added the optional heavy cream.

Over all, I'm quite delighted with the recipe and I would definitely make it again.

Very good. Made for super bowl Sunday for New England patriots. Add a little cayenne pepper for kick and color. Double the recipe. You can use the clam juice from the cans and add bottled clam juice. Did not use the flour as I didn't want the taste. Let simmer for several hours. Thickened up nicely. Serve with crusty French bread.
Super creamy and smooth, but you won't have a big bowl for these portions. Mostly cream, but still delicious! Doesn't taste a lot like clam to be honest though!

I actually left a review asking where the flour was. For corn's sake! I should read the instructions about 10 times evidently. the only thing I did was add celery....or was that in the recipe too? LOL
I used heavy cream and a bottle of clam juice. No milk. I also added a little butter for richness. I used canned potatoes to save time.
Great hearty meal especially for Lenten season. Only change was to add one more can of minced clams and added the juice from the canned clams.
